key_insight: The paper replaces penalty-based QAOA constraint handling with a guarded mixer that keeps personnel-rostering states feasible throughout the quantum evolution.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce tuning burden and improve solution reliability for constrained scheduling by embedding hard coverage and no-consecutive-duty rules directly into the algorithm.
method: Model rostering as a transition graph over feasible binary schedules.
Use a guarded-XY mixer to restrict QAOA dynamics to the fully feasible manifold.
Add a tight-pattern extension for collective exchanges in saturated workload segments where local moves are insufficient.
evidence_signal: Exact statevector simulations on rostering instances show feasible-by-construction evolution, no penalty calibration, and better output concentration than Penalty-X and Coverage-XY under expectation-value and CVaR optimization.
watch_item: The approach is demonstrated in simulation, so practical performance on hardware will depend on circuit depth, connectivity, and noise robustness.
paper_title: Constraint-Preserving QAOA for Personnel Rostering: Coverage-Preserving and Guarded-XY Mixer Constructions
